citation: Olson, C. B., Kim, J. S., Scarcella, R., Kramer, J., Pearson, M., van Dyk, D. A., Collins, P., & Land, R. E. (2012). Enhancing the interpretive reading and analytical writing of mainstreamed English learners in secondary school: Results from a randomized field trial using a cognitive strategies approach. American Educational Research Journal, 49(2), 323-355. https://doi.org/10.3102/0002831212439434
report_number: AERJ 49(2):323-355; IES Grant R305W06016 (The Pathway Project). Extracted from the legal green open-access author/accepted manuscript in Harvard DASH (CC-BY).
design: Multi-site cluster-randomized controlled trial. Assignment level = teacher/classroom: within school-by-grade randomization blocks, secondary English teachers (clusters) in 15 secondary schools (9 middle, 6 high) of Santa Ana Unified School District (SAUSD), CA were randomly assigned to the Pathway Project cognitive-strategies reading/writing PD (treatment) vs business-as-usual district training (control); control teachers received 26h of typical district PD, Pathway teachers received that plus 46h of Pathway PD + coaching. Subject = English Language Arts (interpretive reading + analytical writing) for mainstreamed Latino English learners; grades 6-12 (registry band 7-12). Year 1 baseline n=103 teachers; Year 2 (2008-09, end-of-treatment wave) impact sample n=72 classrooms after teacher attrition (no differential attrition by condition, chi2 p=.26). ALA on-demand writing analysis: 72 classrooms (34 Pathway, 38 control), grades 6-12. CST analysis: 66 classrooms (31 Pathway, 35 control), grades 6-11 (grade 12 excluded because 12th graders do not take the CST). District average class size ~30 students. Impacts estimated with 3-level hierarchical linear models (students within classrooms within school-by-grade blocks), with a classroom-level CST-pretest-mean covariate; ALA and CST scores were normed within grade level so the treatment fixed effect (beta1) is reported directly as a standardized mean difference (Pathway - control).
problems: Effect sizes are model-based standardized mean differences read directly from Table 3 (experimental-teacher sample; the study's headline/confirmatory RQ1 contrast) and Table 4 (all-classrooms extended sample; RQ2). The Pathway fixed effect (beta1) coefficients ARE the standardized mean difference because ALA and CST were normed within grade level (paper, Data Analytic Strategy); the reported s.e. is the HLM model SE and is already cluster-adjusted (3-level model accounting for clustering within teacher/classroom and within school-by-grade block), so cluster_adjusted=true. ICC: the authors did NOT report an empirical design-effect ICC; they only assumed rho=.05/.10 for an a-priori power calculation (endnote 1). I therefore left icc=null (not guessed). n_clusters recorded (classrooms = teachers, 1-to-1). Per-arm and total student n's are not given numerically in the report text/tables (only classroom counts and ~30 students/class average), so n_t/n_c are null. Hedges' J applied with a conservative cluster-based df (n_clusters - 2); at these magnitudes J~0.99 so g~d. g_se=J*se, g_var=g_se^2. The CST Total ELA is a composite that subsumes the CST Reading and CST Writing subtests (which I extracted as subscales). Table 4 rows use the SAME teachers/timepoint but a larger analytic sample (all of each teacher's classroom sections, not just the one study classroom); they are the RQ2 transfer/external-validity estimates, labelled secondary and flagged. Mapping per spec: ALA on-demand analytical writing and CST writing subtest -> Other (writing/language); CST reading subtest and CST Total ELA -> Reading (reading/literacy/ELA). Teacher-practice/implementation outcomes (Pathway Observation Measure, Quality Checklist, teacher-efficacy) were skipped per spec. Year 1 ALA effect (d=.35) and the Year-1-only on-demand replication are noted but the extracted wave is the Year 2 (2008-09) end-of-treatment posttest. SOURCE: journal version is paywalled at SAGE; extracted from the legal green OA accepted manuscript deposited in Harvard DASH (CC-BY, http://nrs.harvard.edu/urn-3:HUL.InstRepos:28552551). No piracy sites used.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Pathway Project cognitive-strategies PD vs business-as-usual control -- Year 2 experimental-teacher sample (headline RQ1)
effect_sizes.test_name: Assessment of Literary Analysis (ALA) on-demand analytical writing assessment, posttest May 2009
effect_sizes.g_method: Table 3 Pathway treatment fixed effect (beta1) = 0.674 with s.e. = 0.128, t = 5.247. ALA was normed within grade level so the coefficient is the standardized mean difference d = 0.674. g = J*d with J = 1 - 3/(4*df-1), df = n_clusters - 2 = 70 (J = 0.98925): g = 0.6668. g_se = J*se = 0.98925*0.128 = 0.1266; g_var = g_se^2 = 0.01603. SE from 3-level HLM -> cluster_adjusted = true; classroom CST-pretest-mean covariate -> pretest_adjusted = true. Standardized within-grade so the standardizing SD is the within-grade SD of the ALA posttest.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 3, ALA column (Pathway treatment effect row); Results RQ1 (p. ~36)
effect_sizes.notes: Study's primary/headline confirmatory outcome; statistically significant (random-effect p<.001; treatment fixed effect t=5.247). On-demand analytical-writing assessment developed by the researchers, scored holistically on a 6-point scale (rubrics adapted from CAHSEE/STAR/NAEP). Grades 6-12, 72 classrooms (34 Pathway, 38 control); ~50% of essays per class scored due to budget. Year 2 (2008-09) replicates the Year 1 ALA effect (d=.35, Kim et al. 2011). Researcher/developer-made -> the meta-analysis (independent measures only) likely excludes this, but extracted per spec instruction to capture all achievement outcomes and label type.
